newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks ease in pre-goliday trade lull.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks ease in pre-goliday trade lull.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed lower Monday after drifting during a session dulled by pre-holiday apathy.

"The market was stagnant, nothing interesting happened. Most dealers have taken positions and are hanging around just in case something happens. They're basically waiting until the new year before they reshuffle portfolios," a trader said.
The blue chip IPC index closed down 12.19 points, or 0.37 percent, at 3,299.17. Volume, at 171.2 million shares traded, was mostly accounted for by cross trades, dealers said.
Most traders said foreign investors were mostly absent.

"There's nothing to say about local investors, because they did nothing and the few that traded just sold some stock to get liquidity and buy presents. We had not a whiff of foreign dealers, They'll be out until the new year," a dealer said.
Dealers also said interest waned after trade balance figures were released and in the run up to inflation figures and the primary auction due later in the day.
The Finance Ministry announced on Sunday a trade surplus of $280 million. Banco de Mexico announced in late trade that consumer prices rose 2.34 percent in the first half of December.

A Reuters survey of money market traders showed an average forecast assigned rate of 27.55 percent for bellwether 28-day Cetes, or Treasury bills, a gain of 0.28 percentage point from last week's rate.
On the broad market, 89 stocks changed hands, of which losers outnumbered gainers by 34 to 29.
Mining company Autlan headed the gainers, up 72 centavos (9 cents) to 7.52 pesos (96 cents), after what traders said was a technical rebound.
Hotel group Posadas fell the most, by 20 centavos (3 cents) to 3.10 pesos (40 cents), but in minimal trade, dealers said.
